STEPPED TEMPLE WITH THE FROG FOUNTAIN: a squat stepped stone temple in deep jungle green, its wide uneven stair climbing to a broad dark doorway, blocks tumbled loose along one flank, worn pictorial reliefs of a carved sun beside the door, a little stone frog fountain sitting crooked at the foot of the stair, half-buried in moss

LOW MOSSY SHRINE ON THE RIVER BEND: a small flat-roofed stone shrine crouching on a mossy bank where the river curves, its single doorway tilted slightly off true, one corner block slumped forward, worn pictorial reliefs of a coiled serpent across the lintel, a carved fish spout dripping into the green water below

STONE GATEWAY IN THE TREES: two massive uneven pillars of different heights carrying a heavy lintel stone, one pillar leaning a few degrees, roots prying between the courses, worn pictorial reliefs of a spread-winged bird across the face, the doorway framing a tunnel of green beyond, a loose drum block tipped at the base

SUNKEN COURTYARD WITH THE FLOWER FLOOR: a broad stone courtyard sunk a full stride below the surrounding jungle floor, its walls uneven and broken at different heights, a mosaic floor of chunky coloured tiles showing a many-petalled flower, one corner stair descending crookedly into the space, a stone basin tilted in the centre

CARVED SPOUT HOUSE OVER THE GREEN POOL: a low open stone pavilion standing over a deep green pool, three surviving pillars of very different heights holding a cracked stone roof with a fourth broken to a stump on one side, worn pictorial reliefs of a leaping fish on each pillar face, a row of carved fish spouts along the sill dripping into the pool below

STAIR DESCENDING INTO CLEAR GREEN: a broad stone stair dropping from a low broken wall straight down into clear shallow water, its steps uneven and scattered with fallen blocks, worn pictorial reliefs of a round moon face on the wall above, a single half-arch standing alone at the water's edge a few strides to one side

WALLS AND ARCHES IN THE SHALLOWS: a stretch of thick stone walls standing waist-deep in bright clear water, two arches of different spans still upright between them, a third arch collapsed to one side, worn pictorial reliefs of a spread-winged bird along the upper course, loose blocks resting on the sandy floor visible through the water

TILTED TOWER IN THE LAGOON: a round stone tower leaning over bright shallow water, its top broken open into three leaning fingers of stone, a broken arch standing alone a few strides off, worn pictorial reliefs of a coiled serpent circling its base, small carved fish spouts along the lower courses, a stone stair running down into the clear green

LEANING PILLARS HALF IN SAND: a loose cluster of stone pillars of very uneven height tilting at different angles, dunes piled to their waists on the windward side, the tallest pillar carrying worn pictorial reliefs of a carved sun near its top, a fallen drum block half-swallowed by sand at the base of the shortest

HALF-BURIED GATEWAY IN THE DESERT: a broad gateway of two massive uneven jambs and a heavy lintel, sand piled to the lintel on one side and dropping away on the other, worn pictorial reliefs of a many-petalled flower carved across the lintel face, a single leaning pillar standing apart to the left, its base buried

FALLEN GIANT IN THE SAND: an enormous stone figure lying on its back in open desert, one arm broken and displaced, the face tipped slightly to one side still wearing a wide carved smile, worn pictorial reliefs of a spread-winged bird along the figure's chest, sand drifting across the lower half in long soft curves

BROKEN KEEP ON THE GREEN HILL: a thick square keep with one wall fallen outward in a tumble of uneven blocks down the slope, the remaining three walls standing at different heights, a round turret stub at one corner still intact, worn pictorial reliefs of a coiled serpent around the doorway arch, a broad stair climbing crookedly to the entrance

ROUND TOWER SPLIT OPEN: a tall round stone tower with its entire east face fallen away, the interior floors visible as broken stone ledges at different heights, moss thick on every course, worn pictorial reliefs of a round moon face above the empty window openings, a tree growing straight up through the hollow centre from the ground

COURTYARD GONE TO GRASS: a wide castle courtyard enclosed by walls of very uneven height, one gateway arch still standing off-centre, its keystone displaced slightly, worn pictorial reliefs of a leaping fish above the arch, a well-head of stacked stone blocks sitting lopsided in the middle of the courtyard, fallen coping stones scattered around it

TILTED STANDING STONES ON THE HEATHER: seven standing stones of very different heights arranged in a rough oval on open moorland, each tilted at its own angle, the tallest carrying worn pictorial reliefs of a carved sun on its flat face, a fallen capstone resting on two shorter uprights at the far end of the oval

FALLEN CAPSTONE ON TWO UPRIGHTS: two stout upright stones of slightly different heights supporting a massive flat capstone tipped at a low angle, the whole arrangement sitting on bare heather, worn pictorial reliefs of a round moon face pressed into the underside of the capstone, three smaller loose stones tumbled nearby at varying distances

CLIFF BUILDINGS ON THE LEDGE: three small stone buildings of very different sizes clinging to a long rock shelf partway up a cliff face, their rooflines at different heights, the largest with a doorway facing outward, worn pictorial reliefs of a spread-winged bird above it, a narrow stone stair connecting the buildings along the shelf

STAIR CUT INTO THE ROCK FACE: a long stone stair cut directly into a cliff, its steps of uneven depth and width climbing in a slight curve, a small landing partway up where a carved niche holds a worn pictorial relief of a coiled serpent, a low stone wall on the open side broken in two places

TINY CHAPEL ON THE PINNACLE: a small stone chapel perched on a narrow rock pinnacle, its single round window still intact, the roof open on one corner where blocks have slid away, worn pictorial reliefs of a many-petalled flower around the window frame, a short bridge of two stone arches connecting the pinnacle to the cliff behind

FLOODED HALL WITH THE LEANING ROOF SLAB: a broad stone hall with green water lying across its floor, seen across one corner, a huge roof slab fallen and leaning against the far end wall as the one dominant mass, three surviving pillars of very different heights clustered to one side of it, worn pictorial reliefs of a leaping fish along the surviving wall frieze, a mosaic of chunky coloured tiles showing a round moon face under the shallow water

ROOFLESS CHAMBER WITH THE STANDING CORNER: a roofless stone chamber seen across one corner, a single surviving corner of wall still at full height carrying a stair that climbs it and stops in mid-air, one tall column leaning well out of true beside it and a broken stump further off, green water covering the floor to ankle depth, worn pictorial reliefs of a carved sun on the standing corner, a broad threshold block tilted at the entrance

TERRACES STEPPING DOWN THE HILLSIDE: broad stone terraces of uneven width descending a green hillside in long steps, a wandering stair cutting off-centre between them, a lopsided gateway standing on the middle terrace, worn pictorial reliefs of a spread-winged bird across its lintel, a giant stone head tipped on its side at the lowest terrace smiling at the sky

HILL CITY WITH THE WANDERING STAIR: a hillside faced with stone terraces of very different heights and depths, the stair between them bending twice and narrowing near the top, a cracked stone basin on the highest terrace fed by a carved fish spout, worn pictorial reliefs of a coiled serpent along the retaining wall of the second terrace

LONG AQUEDUCT STRIDING THE VALLEY: a line of stone arches of uneven span and height crossing a wide green valley, each pier a slightly different thickness, one arch in the middle section collapsed to a rubble heap, worn pictorial reliefs of a many-petalled flower on the pier faces, a short stretch of the water channel on top still intact and open to the sky

AQUEDUCT WITH THE FALLEN ARCH: a stone aqueduct of mismatched arches crossing a valley, the second arch from the left fallen and its stones scattered in a loose fan across the grass below, the remaining arches standing at subtly different heights, worn pictorial reliefs of a round moon face on the tallest standing pier, a bell still hanging in the last intact arch at the far end
